content.title: Boston Marathon 2026 live updates: See how the race unfolded
content.text: 6thinningEntering Monday’s Boston Marathon, the prevailing thought was that we’d see a memorable race. A record perhaps?John Korir delivered, breezing to a 2:01:52 finish to set the course mark on the 130th running of the world’s oldest marathon.His 2026 victory was his second straight in Boston, just like countrywoman Sharon Lokedi, who repeated as the women’s champion.Marcel Hug won his fourth straight men’s wheelchair title and his ninth in 11 years, and Eden Rainbow-Cooper won the women’s wheelchair race — her second victory in Boston.The elite races kicked off a sunlit day along the 26.2-mile course winding from Hopkinton to Boylston Street.2026 Boston Marathon: Big feat, tired feetCrossing the finish line at the 2026 Boston Marathon was a victory within itself. (Video by Jenna Perlman/Globe staff)Along the course, you could spot astronauts and former Bruins, barefooted runners and even a former United States president. There were funny signs — “No matter what,” one read, “you’re faster than the Green Line” — and touching moments as competitors carried their companions over the finish line.Read on to re-live the excitement of the day. See full results here.To continue reading, please login or subscribe to Globe.comGet 6 Months of Unlimited Access for $1What to read next about the Boston MarathonJohn Korir broke the men’s elite course record with a time of 02:01:52, winning his second consecutive Boston Marathon. Read more from John Powers.Sharon Lokedi went back-to-back, championing the women’s elite race with a time of 02:18:50. Read more from Emma Healy.Lokedi and Korir proved to be Marathon favorites in more ways than one. Read Chad Finn’s column from raceday here.Switzerland’s Marcel Hug won the men’s wheelchair race. It’s his fourth straight title and ninth in 11 years. He now has the second-most victories in the race’s history in any division. Great Britain’s Eden Rainbow-Cooper won the women’s wheelchair race. Read more from Michael Silverman.Jess McClain was the top American woman to finish, coming in fifth.
